rubrics_metrics.name: Transcriber convention: capitalization and italics handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The transcriber has attempted to follow Hobbes' original use of capitals and italics closely: restricted full capitalization to places Hobbes used it, except chapter headings which are fully capitalized; where Hobbes used a mixture of full capitalization and italics the transcriber adjusted headings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating or editing this e-text, preserve original capitalization/italics patterns where meaningful and follow the transcriber's convention for headings to keep the text readable in plain ASCII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcriber convention: quoting and quotation marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it is clear italics indicate quoted text, the transcriber introduced quotation marks and retained Hobbes' capitalization within those quotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When converting early-modern printed text to plain ASCII, introduce quotation marks for quoted passages indicated by italics in the original, preserving capitalization inside the quotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcriber convention: italics used for emphasis or proper names
rubrics_metrics.description: Where italics seem used for emphasis, proper names, or other non-quoting uses, the transcriber capitalized the initial letter of those words (rather than marking them as italic), to avoid ugly plain-text markers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This convention favors readability in ASCII e-texts at the cost of losing typographic italic emphasis markers; editors should be consistent and document the choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcriber convention: margin notes and references
rubrics_metrics.description: Margin notes that introduce paragraph subjects or word definitions were included as headers to the paragraph with initial capitals and on a shortened line. Margin references to quotations were included in the text in brackets immediately next to the quotation; square brackets in Hobbes' main text were changed to round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When transcribing marginalia for plain-text e-books, convert them into inline headers or bracketed references near the relevant text to preserve their function as topical markers and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcriber convention: Greek and foreign words
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Greek alphabet the transcriber substituted the nearest ordinary letters and used initial capitals for foreign-language words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To represent non-Latin scripts in ASCII, map characters to visually/phonemically nearest letters and mark foreign words with capitalization to signal language differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcriber convention: fidelity to original spelling/punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: The transcriber reproduced spelling and punctuation exactly except for the introduction of quotation marks; some unavoidable differences from the original were documented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve original orthography and punctuation to retain the flavour/meaning of early texts, but document any systematic changes made for readability or technical constraints.
